newsitem.title: GERMANY: "Wise man" wants no compromises on German tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: "Wise man" wants no compromises on German tax cuts.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl should make "no compromises" on cutting the top tax rate at next week's tax summit with the opposition Social Democrats (SPD), a top economic advisor said on Monday.

The current top rate of 53 percent is hindrance which dissuades foreign firms from investing in Germany, Rolf Peffekoven, a member of Bonn's panel of independent economic advisors, told Saarland Radio.

"I say down with the top tax rate, and I also say the high rates must be lowered to the standard international level and that is clearly under 40 percent," said Peffekoven, who belongs to the panel, also known as the "five wise men".

Kohl's coalition has proposed cutting the top personal income tax rate to 39 percent as part of a 30 billion mark tax cutting package. Some Social Democrats (SPD) want no change in the top rate and deep cuts for middle and low income taxpayers.
But Peffekoven said the reductions sought by the SPD would have little impact on Germany's sluggish economy and unemployment which in January climbed to the highest level since the 1930s.
"We need investments and investments are predominantly financed by those with high incomes," he said.
